gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Sun Gold Power's SGR-8K10E cabin kit ships with two SG48100P batteries that have no self-heating, while the self-heating SGH48100T sells in the same store for $1,035 against $981 (+$54 per battery, +$108 for the kit's two). In an unheated winter cabin the battery choice inside the kit decides whether the system keeps charging, and the default is not the cold-weather battery.
standout_why: ChatGPT got no search results and cited no pages in either chat, so the only rival is ChatGPT's own answer text. Both answers leave the battery generic ('48V-class 100Ah LiFePO4', 'LiFePO4 batteries'). The second answer mentions 'battery temperature protection' once, in a closing question about location. Neither answer names the heated and unheated versions of the same battery, the 5 °C on / 12 °C off heater thresholds, or the price gap. That gives a partial overlap on the general idea and new information on the model, thresholds and price. The finding changes which battery goes in the cart, but I could not open a page showing the unheated battery's low-temperature charge limit, so I scored it 2, not 3.
kit_items: Inverter + panels + battery kit: Sun Gold Power SGR-8K10E (8,000 W 48 V 120/240 V off-grid inverter, 8 × 450 W N-type panels, 2 × SG48100P 51.2 V 100 Ah LiFePO4, 10.24 kWh). Dealectric already lists it, and one store cart holds the whole set.

Battery for an unheated winter cabin: Sun Gold Power SGH48100T (51.2 V 100 Ah, self-heating). The maker says it starts heating below 41 °F (5 °C) and stops at 53.6 °F (12 °C). It costs +$54 per battery over the SG48100P that comes in the kit, and it advertises RS485/CAN for SunGoldPower inverters. Sun Gold Power's T-suffix kits (for example SGR-10K25T) already include it.
Battery for a cabin that stays heated, or one used only in summer: the kit's SG48100P is enough, and its listing names no heating feature.
